_comment: Where one run of price-sync lands, and how each place closes. Read by $GROVE/tools/close.py. This is the list that used to exist only as a sentence inside SKILL.md — a price lives in eight places, and a session that updates five of them and reports 'done' is the failure this file exists to make impossible. Written 2026-09-10 from the skill's own workflow, not from its description.
operates_from: anywhere — the operation spans every place below, so no single one of them is where it 'lives'

state.why: The state reader ships with the skill and is authoritative for the half that matters: it compares prices.json against every document, every .storekit and every page that states a price, which is where every price bug so far came from. close.py runs it rather than re-deriving any of it. The live store read is a separate, optional step — a price that is wrong in the store is rarer than one that is wrong in a file copied from another file.

places.note: prices.json is settled FIRST and is the only file allowed to state a price on its own authority; everything else is propagated from it. Store metadata edited here is a hub change and nothing more until app-store-deliver sends it — and not at all while the version is WAITING_FOR_REVIEW or IN_REVIEW, which would pull the submission out of the queue.

One commit per app repo, in that repo's own terms. A .storekit only drives local StoreKit testing, so a stale one breaks nothing visible — which is exactly why it is the occurrence that gets forgotten.

paths: the pages listed in `site_paths` in prices.json
places.close: commit, then `npm run content`, then `npm run ship`
places.why_enter: Site copy lives in content/en.json, which the site repo's own .claude/owns.json marks `warn`: editing it without running the sync leaves the deployed pages serving the old text. And committing is not publishing here — the site's hosting projects sit on that repo with git deployment switched off, so `npm run ship` is the only thing that puts a price change in front of a customer. This is the place where the twelve-hour wrong price happened.

places.note: Prices ARE editable through the API, and this operation still does not touch them: changing what a customer pays is the owner's decision, not something done while tidying files. Report the misalignment and the exact value; let the owner act.

The API serves GET and HEAD on products and variants — verified, not assumed. There is no write path at all, so this place can only ever be closed by a person at a dashboard. Give them the exact values to type, then re-run the verifier to confirm it landed.

_push_note: A push publishes a whole branch. This operation touches three repos it may not be standing in; it prints what each push would publish and leaves the decision.
order: app-hub (prices.json first — everything else derives from it)
site publish · the two external places (the parts only a person or a separate tool can finish)
_order_why: Content before what points at it. prices.json is the authority, so a document corrected before it is corrected against a number that may still change.
